info.title: Pushpad API
info.description:
The Pushpad API allows you to send web push notifications and manage resources
within your Pushpad account in a simple way using HTTP requests.
All of the functionality that you are familiar with in the Pushpad
dashboard is also available through the API.

get.description:
To list the latest notifications for your project,
send a GET request to `/projects/PROJECT_ID/notifications`.

Only the notifications created in the last 35 days are available.

The response body will be an array containing objects each representing a notification.

200.description: The response is a JSON array of notification objects.

post.description:
To send a web push notification,
send a POST request to `/projects/PROJECT_ID/notifications`.

scheduled.description:
The number of devices the notification will be delivered to.
Note that this value may differ from the number of user IDs (uids) in the request,
for example when some users are not subscribed or are subscribed with multiple devices.
This field is not available for scheduled notifications.

uids.description:
This field is included in the response only if you specify some user IDs (uids) in the request,
and it indicates which of those users are subscribed to notifications.
This field is not available for scheduled notifications.

send_at.description:
The time when the notification will be sent.
Available only for scheduled notifications.

get.description:
To get a notification and its stats,
send a GET request to `/notifications/NOTIFICATION_ID`.

Only the notifications created in the last 35 days are available.

200.description: The response is a JSON object representing a notification.

delete.description:
To cancel a scheduled notification,
send a DELETE request to `/notifications/NOTIFICATION_ID/cancel`.

get.description:
To list all subscriptions in your project,
send a GET request to `/projects/PROJECT_ID/subscriptions`.

The response body will be an array containing objects each representing a subscription.

200.description: The response is a JSON array of subscription objects.

X-Total-Count.description:
The total number of subscriptions for this project
or the number of subscriptions that match the given query
if you set uids or tags in the query string.

post.description:
To create a new subscription,
send a POST request to `/projects/PROJECT_ID/subscriptions`
setting the required attributes.

A subscription will be created using the provided information.
  
The response body will contain a JSON object with the attributes of your new subscription.

This operation is mainly intended to import subscriptions
from another service into Pushpad.

This is not the standard way to collect subscriptions:
usually you collect them using the JavaScript SDK.

get.description:
To show information about an individual subscription,
send a GET request to `/projects/PROJECT_ID/subscriptions/SUBSCRIPTION_ID`.

200.description: The response is a JSON object that contains the subscription attributes.

patch.description:
To update a subscription,
send a PATCH request to `/projects/PROJECT_ID/subscriptions/SUBSCRIPTION_ID`.

The subscription will be updated using the provided information.

The response body will contain a JSON object with the attributes of your subscription.

delete.description:
To delete a subscription,
send a DELETE request to `/projects/PROJECT_ID/subscriptions/SUBSCRIPTION_ID`.

The subscription will be permanently deleted.

A successful request will receive a 204 status code with no body in response.

get.description:
To list all projects in your account, send a GET request to `/projects`.

The response body will be an array containing objects each representing a project.

200.description: The response is a JSON array of project objects.

post.description:
To create a new project, send a POST request to `/projects` setting the
required attributes.

A project will be created using the provided information.

The response body will contain a JSON object with the attributes of your new project.

get.description:
To show information about an individual project, send a GET request
to `/projects/PROJECT_ID`.

200.description: The response is a JSON object that contains the project attributes.

patch.description:
To update a project, send a PATCH request to `/projects/PROJECT_ID`.

The project will be updated using the provided information.

The response body will contain a JSON object with the attributes of your project.

delete.description:
To delete a project, send a DELETE request to `/projects/PROJECT_ID`.

The project will be deleted asynchronously.
The actual processing of the request is performed later.

A successful request will receive a 202 status code with no body in response.

get.description:
To list all senders in your account, send a GET request to `/senders`.

The response body will be an array containing objects each representing a sender.

200.description: The response is a JSON array of sender objects.

post.description:
To create a new sender, send a POST request to `/senders` setting the
required attributes.

A sender will be created using the provided information.

The response body will contain a JSON object with the attributes of your new sender.

get.description:
To show information about an individual sender, send a GET request
to `/senders/SENDER_ID`.

200.description: The response is a JSON object that contains the sender attributes.

patch.description:
To update a sender, send a PATCH request to `/senders/SENDER_ID`.

The sender will be updated using the provided information.

The response body will contain a JSON object with the attributes of your sender.

delete.description:
To delete a sender, send a DELETE request to `/senders/SENDER_ID`.

The sender will be permanently deleted.

You cannot delete a sender if it has associated projects.

A successful request will receive a 204 status code with no body in response.

BearerAuth.description:
Authenticate using an HTTP Bearer token.

Go to Pushpad, Account settings, Access tokens
to create your API key.

Example header: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`

page.name: page
page.description:
If you have many notifications they get paginated and
you need to retrieve them with multiple requests.

parameters_page.name: page
parameters_page.description:
If you have many subscriptions they get paginated and 
you need to retrieve them with multiple requests.

per_page.name: per_page
per_page.description: The number of subscriptions per page.

uids.name: uids[]
uids.description:
Filter subscriptions by user ID.

Subscriptions that have one of these uids associated are returned.

tags.name: tags[]
tags.description:
Filter subscriptions by tags.

Subscriptions that have at least one of these tags associated are returned.

Instead of simple tags, you can also use boolean expressions for tags,
for example: `(tag1 && tag2) || !tag3`.

unauthorized.description: Authentication error, the token is missing or invalid.

forbidden.description: You don't have permission to perform an action or the token has limited access.

server_error.description: A server error or timeout in the processing of the request.

payment_required.description: Action refused due to billing issues, like unpaid invoices.

unprocessable_content.description: Validation error, the request has invalid or missing fields.

too_many_requests.description: Rate limit exceeded, reduce your requests or contact our support.

not_found.description: The resource doesn't exist or no longer exists.

id.description:
A unique identifier for each notification.
This is automatically generated upon notification creation.

project_id.description: The ID of the project the notification belongs to.

title.description: The title of the push notification.

body.example: Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit.
body.description: The main text of the push notification.

target_url.description: The url the user is redirected to when clicks the push notification.

icon_url.description:
The url of an image that will be used as the notification icon.
Suggested size: 192x192px.

badge_url.description:
The url of a small image (that represents the app or the notification category)
that will be displayed when there is not enough space to display the full notification (e.g. Android status bar).
Suggested size: 96x96px.

image_url.description:
The url of an image that will be displayed in the notification content.
Suggested size: 800px for the longer side.

ttl.description:
The number of seconds after which the notification should be dropped
if the device of the user is offline.

require_interaction.description:
Set to true in order to prevent browser from automatically closing the notification after a few seconds.
Currently this applies only to Chrome on desktop.

silent.description: Set to true if you want to disable the notification sound and vibration.

urgent.description:
Set to true for time-sensitive alerts (e.g. incoming phone call)
that must wake up devices that are sleeping.

custom_data.description:
An arbitrary string that represents some metadata that you want to attach to the notification.
This string is passed as an argument to the JavaScript functions binded to the action buttons.

title.description: The label to display on the action button.

target_url.description: The page that opens up when the user clicks the button.

icon.description: The URL of a small icon for the action button.

action.description:
An ID for the action that can be used to trigger a JavaScript callback.
It must be a string of word characters.

actions.description: Add some action buttons to the notification.

starred.description:
Bookmark the notification to make it easier to find it from the Pushpad dashboard.
You can use this feature to highlight some notifications, for example those that have been sent manually.

send_at.description: A time when the notification will be sent.

custom_metrics.description:
Aggregate the stats for this notification into the specified buckets (you can add up to 3 buckets for a single notification).
Custom metrics are a way to aggregate the stats for all the notifications that belong to a given category.
You need to explicitly create the categories from the project settings before using this feature.
You can learn more in the Monitoring section of the documentation.

uids.description:
The users that should receive this push notification.
When the field is omitted or null, it is ignored and the push notification is sent to everyone or to the people specified by tags.
When the field is an empty array, the notification will not be sent to anyone.

tags.description:
The segments that should receive this push notification (i.e. the browsers that have at least one of these tags associated will receive the notification).
If both uids and tags are present, only the browsers that match both the conditions will receive the notification (i.e. a browser must be associated to a user ID listed in uids and have at least one of those tags).
Instead of simple tags, you can pass boolean expressions that use the operators !, &&, || (from highest to lowest precedence) and can include parentheses.
If you pass an array of tags and boolean expressions they are interpreted as ||: the example above is equivalent to "tag0 || tag1 || tagA && !tagB".
When the field is omitted or null, it is ignored and the push notification is sent to everyone or to the people specified by uids.
When the field is an empty array, the notification will not be sent to anyone.

created_at.description:
A time value given in ISO 8601 format.
It represents when the notification was created.

successfully_sent_count.description: The number of notifications that were sent successfully by Pushpad.

opened_count.description: The number of notifications that were clicked or opened.

scheduled_count.description: The number of deliveries that are still in the sending queue.

scheduled.description:
The deliveries have not started yet.
You can try to cancel a notification that is in this status.

cancelled.description:
The notification has been cancelled.
A notification can be cancelled on purpose or it can be cancelled by the system (for example if you exceed the usage quota).

id.description:
A unique identifier for each subscription.
This is automatically generated upon subscription creation.

project_id.description: The ID of the project the subscription belongs to.

endpoint.description:
The push endpoint of a browser, as described in the W3C Push API.
It is a URL where the application can deliver the push notifications 
that should be sent to the browser.
An endpoint uniquely identifies the subscription.

p256dh.description:
The p256dh property of the push subscription object, as described in the W3C Push API.
It is an elliptic curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH) public key associated with the push subscription.

auth.description:
The auth property of the push subscription object, as described in the W3C Push API.
It is an authentication secret that an application server uses in authentication of its messages.

uid.description:
A user identifier associated with the subscription.
You can use it to find the push subscription of a user 
and then send notifications to that specific user.
You can choose any ID that makes sense for your application,
like the ID of the user in your database.

tags.description:
Tags associated with the subscription.
You can use them to filter the push subscriptions
and send notifications to a segment of your audience.
You can add all tags that make sense for your application.

last_click_at.description:
A time value given in ISO 8601 format.
It represents the last time that a notification sent to this subscription
was clicked by the user.
If there aren't any clicks on notifications yet, null is returned.

created_at.description:
A time value given in ISO 8601 format.
It represents when the subscription was created.

id.description:
A unique identifier for each project.
This is automatically generated upon project creation.

sender_id.description: The ID of the sender associated to this project.

name.description: The human-readable name set for the project.

website.description:
The URL of the project.
This is also the default URL for notifications.

icon_url.description:
The default icon for notifications.
Suggested size >= 192x192px, squared.

badge_url.description:
A small icon displayed in the status bar for notifications.
Suggested size >= 96x96px, squared.

notifications_ttl.description: Drop the notifications that cannot be delivered within this amount of time.

notifications_require_interaction.description:
Turn on this option to require user interaction and prevent browser from 
automatically closing the notifications after a few seconds.

notifications_silent.description: Turn on this option to disable the sound and vibration of notifications.

created_at.description:
A time value given in ISO 8601 format.
It represents when the project was created.

id.description:
A unique identifier for each sender.
This is automatically generated upon sender creation.

name.description: The human-readable name set for the sender.

vapid_private_key.description:
The VAPID private key used to sign notifications.
This is automatically generated upon sender creation.
You can optionally provide it if you want to import your existing key.

vapid_public_key.description:
The VAPID public key associated to the subscriptions.
This is automatically generated upon sender creation.
You can optionally provide it if you want to import your existing key.

created_at.description:
A time value given in ISO 8601 format.
It represents when the sender was created.

tags.name: Notifications
tags.description:
A notification is a web push notification sent with Pushpad.

A notification includes some content (title, body, image, etc.),
the target URL that is opened after a click, and many other options.

You can create notifications that are sent immediately 
or scheduled notifications that are sent in the future.

A notification can be sent to all subscribers or to some of them,
by using the targeting options (uids and tags).

You can also get stats about the sending status and clicks for each notification.
Or you can aggregate the stats for many notifications using the custom metrics.

By sending requests to the Notifications endpoint, you can
create, read or delete notifications.

tags.name: Subscriptions
tags.description:
A subscription is a subscription to notifications.

You have a subscription for each browser that receives your push notifications.

A subscription includes the endpoint (URL) and keys used to send the notifications
to a browser. It can also include optional data, like a user ID (uid) and 
tags that can be used to find that subscription and send notifications to
that subscriber.

By sending requests to the Subscriptions endpoint, you can
create, read, update or delete subscriptions.

tags.name: Projects
tags.description:
A project is a project on Pushpad.

A project includes notifications, subscriptions, settings and stats.

Usually you have a project for each website that sends notifications.
A domain can also use multiple projects,
but they must be associated to the same sender.

You can add multiple members with limited access to a project.

By sending requests to the Projects endpoint, you can
create, read, update or delete projects.

tags.name: Senders
tags.description:
A sender is the owner of the subscriptions and the signer of the notifications.

It includes the VAPID keys used for Web Push.

Each sender can have one or more projects.

By sending requests to the Senders endpoint, you can
create, read, update or delete senders.
